abstract:
Let $C \to B$ be a Galois cover of curves with group $G$, varying in a Hurwitz family, and let $V$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ whose character field is an imaginary quadratic field $K$ and which is realized over $K$. The $V$-isotypic part of $H^1(C)$ is then a family of $K$-Hodge structures. When its Hodge numbers are balanced, $(m, m)$, it is of Weil type and gives Weil classes on abelian varieties of dimension $2m$. Several recent constructions of algebraic Weil classes start from such a family whose period image is open, or a hypersurface, in the unitary period domain; this paper calls such a family a "source".

We classify sources for $m = 4$ under the hypothesis that the primitive part of the monodromy contains a pseudo-reflection. Then $K$ is $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ or $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$, and the monodromy is $W(E_8)\cdot\mu_k$ ($k = 3, 4$), $G_{33}$ or $G_{34}$, with forced local data. Without the pseudo-reflection hypothesis, a source needs a primitive monodromy group of degree at least $23$. This uses a theorem of Guralnick and Tiep.

For $m = 3$ (Weil sixfolds), in the reflection case and without field descent, the only fields other than $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ and $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$ are $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-7})$, from $G_{24}$, and $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-2})$, from a group $G_F = \langle W(F_4), i\varphi/\sqrt{2}\rangle$ of order $2304$ that we construct. Every balanced family in either group has split discriminant. So in the reflection case, without descent, these covers cannot produce nonsplit Weil sixfolds over any new field. In the reflection-free case without descent, a source over a new field needs a primitive monodromy group of degree at least $14$. Galois descent is excluded except for twisted deleted permutation modules, which remain open.

change_summary:
Version 2 makes only the four minor improvements requested in the v1 review. No hypothesis, theorem statement, proof step or certificate result is changed.
(1) Theorem A now says explicitly that its list contains necessary possibilities only, and that existence and the required period dimension are not claimed for every case. Proposition 6.1 now separates the $9$-dimensional Hurwitz space (the dimension count required by (H3)) from dominance, which it states is not claimed and is not needed for Theorem C.
(2) Section 5 defines age, $\mathrm{age}^*$ and junior elements at first use, following [12, Def. 2.1 and §2]. A new paragraph before Remark 5.3 recalls $V_g$, $k(g)$, $\Theta(g)$, $\delta(g)$ and $q(g)$ from [5, §2], with the hypotheses under which they are defined (positive-definite form, finite order, $\det_K = \pm 1$), and how the discriminant of a balanced family reduces to the product of the $q(C_j)$ modulo norms [5, Thms 2.1(2), 2.2(3)]. It also defines "universally split". In Remark 5.3, $k$ is now written $k(C)$. The supplement's README and prop52_details.md now use LaTeX math; a word-level comparison shows only notation changes plus one sentence identifying [GT3] and [GT12] with references [15] and [12].
(3) New certificate certs/f4tuple_explicit.{g,out}. It hard-codes one tuple $(R^{10}, O, O)$ in $G_F$ (ten roots of $F_4$ and two outer involutions with entries in $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-2})$) and verifies, without search, that its product is $1$, that it generates $G_F$ (order $2304$), that its rank sum is $14$, that its Hodge numbers are $(3,3)$, and that $N' - 3 = 9$. Proposition 6.1 cites it. The README now says that f4tuple.g is a randomized search whose trial and hit counts can vary. It also lists what else can differ on a rerun. We reran every certificate before submitting. The differences from the stored outputs were GAP syntax-warning messages (file paths and echoed source lines) and, in u52q2.out, the order of the class lines and the exact values of $q(C)$. These values change by norms because GAP picks class representatives at random. Running u52norm.py on the new output gives the same norm classification.
(4) The abstract's opening now states that $V$ is realized over $K$ and that the Weil structure requires balanced Hodge numbers $(m, m)$, consistent with (H2).

coauthors.contribution: Supplied the finite-order trace argument and the tensor-conjugacy step for the tensor-induced case of Proposition 5.2, the GT12 Section 5.2 route for the extraspecial 2^{1+6} case, and the corrected scalar-order patterns in Section 7; pointed to Guralnick-Tiep Cor. 1.6 and checked GT3 Prop. 2.8, Marin-Michel normalizers and the hypotheses of p58 Thm 2.2(3) in the primary sources; audited Lemmas 3.5 and 7.1 and two review packets, and independently reran the U5(2).2 certificates.
